senses.gloss:
दक दक, अम्, n. = उदक (the initial vowel
being dropped), water.
—दक-लावणिक, अस्, ई, अम्
(fr. दक+लवण), prepared with water and salt.
—दकोदर (˚क-उद्˚), अम्, n. (instead of उद-
कोदर, cf. उदकोदरिन्), a watery or dropsical belly.

दाक, अस्, m. a giver, donor, one who makes
presents, especially to Brāhmans; the institutor of
a sacrifice who employs and pays the officiating
priests.
दाक दाक. See under. rt. 1. दा.

दक्ष् दक्ष्, cl. 1. P. A. दक्षति, -ते,
ददक्ष, दक्षितुम्, Ved. to act to the
satisfaction of another (with dat. in P.); to be
competent, be able, be strong or powerful (A.); to
grow, increase; to do or act quickly, go, move;
to hurt, kill: Caus. P. दक्षयति, -यितुम्, Aor.
अददक्षत्, to make able or strong.

दक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, able, fit, competent, suitable,
adroit, expert, clever, judicious, dexterous [cf. Gr.
δεξιός]; intelligent, upright, honest; (अस्), m. epi-
thet of Soma (as heightening or strengthening the
intellectual faculties; according to Sāy. = वृद्ध);
epithet of Śiva; epithet of the Ganges (as satisfying
or suiting all); ability, power, fitness; capacity,
intellectual ability, mental power, talent; strength of
[]
will, energy, will, disposition; (in the Veda दक्ष
and क्रतु, i. e. energy and intelligence, are often
joined together as the chief two faculties of the
mind, cf. क्रतु); bad disposition, evil design; N.
of an Āditya; a creative power associated with
Aditi, and therefore sometimes identified with Prajā-
pati; (his daughter is called Kṛttikā: in the Post-
vedic literature Dakṣa is the subject of numerous
legends, which relate his history differently; he is
there generally called the son of Brahmā, and placed
among the Prajā-patis or at their head as ‘the lord
of all creatures,’ being born from Brahmā's right
thumb, as his wife was from the left, see Manu IX.
128: in other legends he is said to be the son of
the ten Pra-cetasas or of Pra-cetas alone, whence his
patronymic Prācetasa; he is variously stated to have
had fifty, sixty, forty-four, and a less number of
daughters, of whom twenty-seven became the wives
of the Moon, forming the lunar asterisms, and thir-
teen or, according to others, seventeen or only eight
the wives of Kaśyapa, becoming by this latter the
mothers of gods, demons, men, and animals: Dakṣa
on one occasion celebrated a great sacrifice to obtain
a son, but omitted to invite Śiva who, according to
one legend, was his son-in-law, (Śiva's wife being Satī,
a form of Durgā, daughter of Dakṣa); this irritated
the god, who interrupted the sacrifice and decapitated
his father-in-law, see दक्षाध्वर-ध्वंश-कृत्:
Dakṣa is sometimes regarded as an Avatār of
Brahmā himself, and is even in one legend identified
with Viṣṇu); N. of a son of Garuḍa; N. of a man
with the patronymic Pārvati; of a Muni and legis-
lator; of a prince or a son of Uśīnara; of one of the
five Brāhmans of Kānya-kubja, from whom the
Brāhmans of Bengal are said to have sprung; (ac-
cording to the lexicographers also) the bull of Śiva;
a cock; a kind of plant; a name of Agni or fire;
a general lover, one attached to many mistresses; (आ),
f. the earth; [cf. अतूर्त-दक्ष, दीन-द्˚, &c.: cf. also
दक्षिण; Gr. δεξιός, δεξιτερός; Lat. dex-ter, dex-
timus; Goth. taihsvs; Angl. Sax. teso; Old Germ.
zeso; Hib. deas, ‘right, southern.’]
—दक्ष-कन्या,
f. ‘daughter of Dakṣa,’ (especially) epithet of Durgā,
the wife of Śiva.
—दक्ष-क्रतु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved.
having a strong will or intelligence, having a clear
understanding.
—दक्ष-जा, f. ‘daughter of Dakṣa,’
the goddess Durgā; a lunar asterism; [cf. दक्ष.]
—दक्षजा-पति, इस्, m. ‘the husband of the
daughters of Dakṣa,’ an epithet of the Moon; also
of Śiva.
—दक्ष-ता, f. or दक्ष-त्व, अम्, n.
dexterity, cleverness, ability.
—दक्ष-ताति, इस्, f.,
Ved. mental power or capacity.
—दक्ष-निधन,
अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
—दक्ष-पति, इस्, m., Ved.
lord of the faculties, lord of power or might; pro-
tector of the sacrifice.
—दक्ष-पितृ, ता, त्री, तृ,
Ved. having Dakṣa as father or progenitor, (the m.
pl. may be either दक्ष-पितरस् or -पितारस्); pre-
serving, possessing or granting abilities.
—दक्ष-
मख-मथन, अम्, n. ‘destruction of Dakṣa's
sacrifice,’ N. of the ninety-seventh and ninety-eighth
chapters of the Liṅga-Purāṇa.
—दक्ष-यज्ञ, अस्,
m. the sacrifice celebrated by Dakṣa.
—दक्ष-
यज्ञ-भङ्ग, अस्, m. the interruption of Dakṣa's
sacrifice.
—दक्षयज्ञ-विध्वंस, अस्, m. ‘de-
struction of Dakṣa's sacrifice,’ N. of the fifteenth
chapter of the Kūrma-Purāṇa.
—दक्षयज्ञ-वि-
ध्वंसन, अम्, n., N. of the fifth chapter of the
Śṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa.
—दक्षय-
ज्ञ-विनाशिनी, f. ‘destroyer of the sacrifice of Dakṣa,’
an epithet of Durgā.
—दक्ष-विहिता, f. (scil. गा-
था), a hymn or song arranged by Dakṣa.
—द-
क्ष-वृध्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. rejoicing in power or
energy &c.
—दक्ष-शाप, अस्, m. ‘the curse of
Dakṣa,’ N. of the thirty-third chapter of the
Svarga-khaṇḍa or third part of the Padma-Purāṇa.
—दक्ष-साधन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. effective
of energy, inspiring courage.
—दक्ष-सावर्णि,
इस्, m., N. of the ninth Manu.
—दक्ष-सुत,
अस्, m. the son of Dakṣa (?); (आ), f. a daughter
of Dakṣa, a lunar asterism or one of the wives
of the Moon.
—दक्षाध्वर-ध्वंश-कृत्
[]
(˚क्ष-अध्˚), त्, m. ‘disturber of the sacrifice of
Dakṣa,’ a N. of Śiva; (Dakṣa having instituted
a sacrifice to which he invited all the gods except
his son-in-law Śiva and his wife Satī, the latter went
unbid, and being received contemptuously, threw
herself into the fire; upon which an emanation or
incarnation of Śiva was produced, named Vīra-bha-
dra, who attacked Dakṣa, and a general affray
ensued in which the gods and Ṛṣis took the part
of Dakṣa, but were wounded and dispersed: Dakṣa
himself was decapitated, but was restored to life by
Śiva at the prayer of the gods; the decapitated head,
however, was not to be found, and the head of a ram
had therefore to be substituted for the one lost.)
—द-
क्षेश्वर-लिङ्ग (˚क्ष-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga.

दाक्ष दाक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दक्ष), relat-
ing to Dakṣa; relating to Dākṣi; (अस्), m. or
(अम्), n. the south; दाक्षस्यायनम् (˚य-अय्˚)
= दक्षिणायनम्, the progress of the sun towards
the south; the winter solstice; the sacrifice per-
formed at this time; (आस्), m. pl., N. of the disciples
of a particular school.

दक्षस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. = दक्ष, able, strong,
dexterous, &c.

दक्षाय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be satisfied or
pleased; (Sāy.) increaser of all; to be honoured, to
be augmented (by oblations); (अस्), m. a vulture;
an epithet of Garuḍa or the bird of Viṣṇu.

दाक्षाय्य दाक्षाय्य, अस्, m. a vulture; [cf.
दक्षाय्य.]

दक्षिण, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Pāṇ. I. 1,
34, and VII. 1, 16, can only be declined as a
pronominal when it denotes relative position, i. e.
‘situated on the right hand’ or ‘southern,’ and
even in this sense can be optionally declined like
शिव in abl. loc. sing. m. n. and nom. voc. pl. m.;
but दक्षिणायां दिशि, for the loc. f. in Hari-vaṃśa
12390, is against the rule), able, competent, clever,
skilful, dexterous [cf. दक्ष]; right (not left;
probably applied to the right hand, foot, &c., as the
cleverest or most skilful), situated on the right side,
(opposed to सव्य, वाम; दक्षिणम् परी, to
walk round a person with the right side towards
him; दक्षिणं कृ, to place on the right side,
to turn the right side towards a person as a mark of
respect); south, southern (as being on the right side
of a person looking towards the east), situated to
the south, turned or directed southward, (दक्षिणा
दिश्, the south, the southern quarter or point of the
compass; दक्षिणस्यां दिशि, in the southern
quarter; दक्षिण आम्नायस्, the southern sacred
text, one of the holy texts of the Tāntrikas); straight-
forward, candid, sincere, upright, honest, impartial;
pleasing, amiable, compliant; submissive, dependent,
subject; (अस्), m. the right (hand or arm); the
right hand horse, the horse on the right side of the
pole of a carriage; an epithet of Śiva; (अस्, अम्),
m. n. the right side; सव्यं दक्षिणम् एव च,
to the left and to the right; the south, the country
of the south, the Dekhan; (आ), f., scil. गो, a prolific
cow, ‘able to calve and give milk,’ a good milch-
cow; a present to Brāhmans or young virgins (con-
sisting originally of a cow, and given upon solemn
or sacrificial occasions); property so acquired [cf.
Manu VIII. 349]; Donation to Brāhmans personified
as a goddess, (generally mentioned together with
Brahmaṇas-pati, Soma, Indra, &c., and said to be
the authoress of Ṛg-veda X. 107; sometimes re-
garded as a daughter of Prajā-pati, or as the wife of
Sacrifice personified, or as born from Kṛṣṇa's right
side, or as the wife of Ruci); wages or remunera-
tion in general; a fee, gift, donation (e. g. प्राण-
दक्षिणा, the gift of life); offering, oblation in
general; completion of any rite, fixing or establish-
ing any act or place; scil. दिश्, the south; the
southern quarter, the southern point of the compass,
the Dekhan; a form or figure of Durgā, in which
the right side is said to be advanced; (अम्), n. the
right hand or highest doctrine of the Śāktas; द-
क्षिणा or दक्षिणेन, ind. on the right, on the
right side of (with acc. and gen.); on the south,
southward; दक्षिणेन कृ, to place on the right,
to leave on the right; दक्षिणात्, ind. on the
right, from the south, southward; दक्षिणे, ind.
on the right, on the south, southward; [cf. Lith.
dészinê, f. ‘the right hand,’ = perhaps Russ. yug,
‘south;’ yuṣnyĭ, ‘southern.’]
—दक्षिण-कालिका,
f. a form of Durgā worshipped by the Tāntrikas.
—दक्षिण-तस्, ind. from the right, to the right
hand; from the south, southward, southerly; द-
[]
क्षिणतः कृ, to turn the right side towards a
person (as a mark of respect); to stand on the
right side of any one and so assist him; दक्षिण-
तः पुरस्तात् or दक्षिणतः पुरः, to the south-
east, on the south-east.
—दक्षिणतस्-कपर्द or
दक्षिणा-कपर्द, आस्, m. pl., Ved. ‘wearing the
hair knotted or braided on the right side of the
head,’ epithet of the Vasiṣṭhas.
—दक्षिण-त्रा,
ind., Ved. on the right side.
—दक्षिण-त्व, अम्,
n. uprightness, honesty.
—दक्षिण-धुरीण, अस्,
आ, अम्, harnessed on the right side of the pole of a
carriage.
—दक्षिण-पथ, a wrong reading for
दक्षिणा-पथ, q. v.
—दक्षिण-पश्चात्, ind. to
the south-west, on the south-west.
—दक्षिण-
पश्चार्ध (˚च-अर्˚), अस्, m. the south-western side.
—दक्षिण-पश्चिम, अस्, आ, अम्, south-western.
—दक्षिण-पाञ्चालक, अस्, इका, अम्, relating to
the southern Pañcālas.
—दक्षिण-पूर्व, अस्, आ,
अम्, south-eastern; (आ), f., scil. दिश्, the south-east
quarter; (एण), ind. to the south-east of (with acc.).
—दक्षिण-प्राञ्च्, आङ्, आची, आक्, south-eastern; द-
क्षिण-प्राची, f. the south-east quarter.
—दक्षिण-
भाग, अस्, m. the southern hemisphere.
—दक्षि-
ण-मानस, N. of a place of pilgrimage.
—दक्षि-
ण-मारुत, अस्, m. the south wind.
—दक्षिण-
सद् or दक्षिणा-सद्, त्, त्, त्, sitting or remaining
seated on the right or southern side.
—दक्षिण-
स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing upon the right, to the
south, &c.; (अस्), m. a charioteer (as standing
on the right of his master; cf. सव्ये-ष्ठ).
—दक्षिणा-कपर्द, see दक्षिणतस्-कपर्द.
—दक्षिणा-काल, अस्, m. the time of (receiving)
the sacrificial gift or fee.
—दक्षिणाग्नि (˚ण-अग्˚),
इस्, m. the southern fire of the altar, a sacred fire
placed towards the south, (in the Brāhmaṇas generally
called Anvāhārya-pacana.)
—दक्षिणाग्र (˚णा-
अग्र), अस्, आ, अम्, pointing to the south, having
the head or point turned towards the south.
—द-
क्षिणाचल (˚ण-अच्˚), अस्, m. the southern moun-
tain, the Malaya range.
—दक्षिणाचार (˚ण-आच्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, honest or upright in conduct, well-
behaved; a worshipper of Śakti according to the
purer or right hand ritual.
—दक्षिणाचारिन्, ई, इणी,
इ, a worshipper of Śakti according to the purer or
right hand ritual; a follower of the right hand
Śākta system.
—दक्षिणा-ज्योतिस्, इस्, इस्, इस्, Ved.
brilliant by the sacrificial gift.
—दक्षिणाञ्च् (˚ण-
अञ्च्), आङ्, आची, आक्, turned to the south, southward.
—दक्षिणात्यय (˚ण-अत्˚), अस्, m. one who
goes beyond the south, a dweller in the south.
—दक्षिणा-द्वार, अस्, आ, अम्, having the door
on the south.
—दक्षिणान्तिका (˚ण-अन्˚), f. a
kind of metre.
—दक्षिणा-पथ, अस्, m. the path
or road of the Dakṣiṇā, i. e. of the cow constituting
the sacrificial fee (situated between the Śālā and the
Sadas); the southern region or country, the De-
khan.
—दक्षिणापथ-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going to
the south, living in the south.
—दक्षिणापथ-जन्-
मन्, आ, m. born in the south, a southern; (-जन्मा-
नस्), m. pl., N. of the Andhakas, Guhas, Pulindas, Sava-
ras, Cucukas, and Madrapas, all outcast or barbarous
tribes.
—दक्षिणा-पथिक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging
to the southern region.
—दक्षिणापर (˚ण-अप्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, south-western.
—दक्षिणा-प्रवण,
अस्, आ, अम्, shelving or inclining to the south.
—द-
क्षिणा-प्रष्टि, इस्, m., Ved. the horse harnessed on
the right side of the yoke-horses (युग्य); [cf. Gr.
δεξιόσειρος.]
—दक्षिणा-बन्ध, अस्, m. (in the
Sāṅkhya phil.) N. of one of the three states of bondage,
the bondage of ritual observance; [cf. दाक्षिण and
दाक्षिणिक.]
—दक्षिणाभिमुख (˚णा-अभ्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, facing southwards, directed southwards,
flowing southwards.
—दक्षिणाभिमुख-स्थित,
अस्, आ, अम्, standing with the face southwards.
—द-
क्षिणा-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, turning the face to the
right or to the south, facing south.
—दक्षिणा-
मूर्ति, इस्, m. one of the forms of Śiva with the
Tāntrikas; N. of an author.
—दक्षिणामूर्ति-
प्रयोग, अस्, m., N. of a chapter of the Tantra-
sāra.
—दक्षिणामूर्ति-मन्त्र, अस्, m., N. of a
chapter of the Śāradātilaka by Lakṣmaṇa.
—द-
[]
क्षिणामूर्ति-संहिता, f., N. of a chapter of the
Tantra-sāra.
—दक्षिणामूर्त्य्-उपनिषद्, त्, f., N.
of an Upaniṣad.
—दक्षिणायन (˚ण-अय्˚), अम्,
n. the sun's progress south of the equator, the winter's
solstice, the half-year in which the sun moves from
north to south; दक्षिणायनम् अनुया, to follow
the southward way, to go to Yama's quarter, i. e. to
die; (अस्, आ, अम्), situated in the sun's course from
north to south (said of certain asterisms).
—द-
क्षिणा-युग्य, अस्, m. the right yoke-horse.
—द-
क्षिणारण्य (˚ण-अर्˚), अम्, n. the southern forest,
N. of a particular forest (probably in the Dekhan).
—दक्षिणारुस् (˚ण-अर्˚), उस्, उस्, उस्, wounded on
the right side.
—दक्षिणार्ध (˚ण-अर्˚), अस्, m.
the right side, the southern side.
—दक्षिणार्ध्य,
अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the preceding), Ved. situated on the
right, being on the southern side.
—दक्षिणार्ह
(˚णा-अर्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, deserving a fee, meriting a
reward, worthy of a gift.
—दक्षिणा-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत् (fr. दक्षिण with lengthening of the final), Ved.
able, competent, strong, fit, effective; (fr. दक्षि-
णा), giving sacrificial presents, offering large remu-
neration, abounding in presents, possessed of a gift,
having ample rewards, piously disposed.
—दक्षिणा-
वर्त (˚णा-आव्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, turning to the right,
turned towards the south; दक्षिणावर्त आदित्यस्,
the sun in his course from the north to the south;
(अस्), m. the southern country, the Dekhan, a conch-
shell with the valve opening to the right.
—दक्षि-
णावर्तक (˚णा-आव्˚), अस्, इका, अम्, turning to the
right, turned towards the south; (अकी), f., N. of a
plant or shrub (= वृश्चि-कालि); a line of bees.
—दक्षिणा-वह्, -वाट्, Ved. ‘being borne to the right
or to the south of the (Āhavanīya) fire,’ epithet of the
sacrificial ladle.
—दक्षिणावृत् (˚णा-आव्˚), त्, त्, त्, Ved.
turned towards the right, going round on the right.
—दक्षिणाशा (˚ण-आशा), f. the southern quarter,
the south.
—दक्षिणाशा-पति, इस्, m. ‘the lord of
the south,’ epithet of Yama.
—दक्षिणाशा-रति, इस्,
m. (? रति for पति), an epithet of Agastya.
—द-
क्षिणा-सद्, see दक्षिण-सद्.
—दक्षिणेतर
(˚ण-इत्˚), different from the right, other than the
right, the left.
—दक्षिणेर्मन् (˚ण-ईर्मन् = 2.
ईर्म), आ, आ, अ, wounded on the right side or right fore
leg (as a deer). (In any other sense this compound
takes the form दक्षिणेर्म, अस्, आ, अम्, e. g. द-
क्षिणेर्मं शकटम्, a cart broken on the right
side.)
—दक्षिणोत्तर (˚ण-उत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, situ-
ated on the right and left, lying to the south and
north, turned to the south and north.
—दक्षि-
णोत्तर-वृत्त, the meridian line.
—दक्षिणोत्त-
रिन् (˚ण-उत्˚), ई, इणी, इ, Ved. being above on the
right side, overhanging on the right side.
दक्षिण दक्षिण. See col. 1.

दक्षिणा, दक्षिणेन, दक्षिणे. See col. 1,
under दक्षिण.

दाक्षिण दाक्षिण, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दक्षिणा),
belonging or relating to a sacrificial gift or to a gift
in general; relating or belonging to the south;
(अम्), n. a collection of sacrificial gifts; (आनि), n.
pl., N. of a Kāṇḍa in the Taittirīya-saṃhitā.
—दा-
क्षिणशाल, अस्, &c. (fr. दक्षिण + शाला), relating
to a hall or room situated to the south.

दक्षिणाहि, ind. far on the right, far in the
south (with abl.).

दक्षिणित्, त्, ind., Ved. on the right hand, to the
right; [cf. प्र-दक्षिणित्.]

दक्षिणी-कृ, cl. 5. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्-
तुम्, to place on the right hand, to turn the right
side towards any one (acc.), to walk round a person
with the right side turned towards him (as a mark
of respect).
—दक्षिणी-कृत्य, ind. having walked
round in the above manner.

दक्षिणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, worthy of the sacrificial
fee, meriting a reward, fit for a sacrificial donation,
worthy to be honoured with presents; [cf. आ-दक्षि-
णीय and दक्षिण्य.]
दाक्षिणीय = दक्षिणीय.

दक्षिण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = दक्षिणीय, merit-
ing a sacrificial reward &c.; [cf. दाक्षिण्य.]

1. दाक्षिण्य, अस्, &c. (fr. दक्षिणा), belonging
or relating to a sacrificial gift; meriting a sacrificial
gift or reward.

दक्षि दक्षि or दक्षिन् (fr. 1. दह्), Ved.
burning, blazing; (according to Sāy. = धक्षि),
thou burnest. (In Ṛg-veda I. 141, 8, दक्षि =
दहति.)

दाक्षि, इस्, m. a son of Dakṣa; (ई), f. a daughter
[]
of Dakṣa.
—दाक्षि-कन्था, f., N. of a village in
the north of India in the country of the Vāhlikas
or Balkh.
—दाक्षिकन्थीय, अस्, आ, अम्, produced
or born in Dākṣi-kanthā, relating to Dākṣi-kanthā.
—दाक्षि-कर्ष, अस्, m., N. of a village.
—दा-
क्षिकार्षुक, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from or relating
to Dākṣi-karṣa.
—दाक्षि-कूल, अम्, n., N. of a
village.
—दाक्षि-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village.
—दाक्षिग्रामीय, अस्, आ, अम्, coming from or
relating to Dākṣi-grāma.
—दाक्षि-नगर, अम्,
n., N. of a town.
—दाक्षि-पलद and दाक्षि-
प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of places.
—दाक्षि-ह्रद,
अस्, m., N. of a lake.
—दाक्षिह्रदीय, अस्, आ, अम्,
relating to the above lake.
—दाक्षी-पुत्र, अस्, m.
‘the son of Dākṣī,’ Pāṇini.

दाक्षक, अस्, &c., inhabited by the Dākṣis;
(अम्), n. a multitude of the descendants of Dakṣa.

दाक्षायण, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from the
Dakṣa family, of or relating to Dakṣa; (अस्), m.
a son or distant descendant of Dakṣa; a particular
kind of sacrifice [cf. दाक्षायण-यज्ञ]; (ई), f., N. of
any of the daughters of Dakṣa; of Aditi; of Diti; of
Kadrū; of Vi-natā; of the nymph and asterism
Rohiṇī; of Su-rasā, mother of the Nāgas; of Jayā
and Vi-jayā; of Svadhā; of Durgā, wife of Śiva; of
the wife of Dharma, mentioned in the Vāmana-
Purāṇa; N. of the plant Croton Polyandrum, =
दन्ती; (ण्यस्), f. pl. the twenty-seven lunar man-
sions considered mythologically as the daughters of
Dakṣa and wives of the Moon; (अम्), n. the pos-
terity of Dakṣa; gold or a gold ornament (as an
ear-ring &c.); = दाक्षस्यायनम्, the winter sol-
stice; the sacrifice performed at this time.
—दा-
क्षायण-भक्त, अम्, n. the district inhabited by
the Dākṣas.
—दाक्षायण-यज्ञ, अस्, m., N. of
a kind of sacrifice said to be a modification of the
Darśapaurṇamāsa (extending through fifteen instead
of thirty years).
—दाक्षायणयज्ञिक, अस्, आ, अम्,
or दाक्षायणयज्ञिन्, ई, इनी, इ, belonging to the
Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice.
—दाक्षायणी-प, अस्, or दा-
क्षायणी-पति, इस्, m. ‘husband of Dākṣāyaṇī,’
epithet of the Moon; of Śiva.
—दाक्षायणी-र-
मण, अस्, m. ‘delighting in Dākṣāyaṇī,’ epithet
of the Moon.
—दाक्षायण्य्-अग्नि-प्रवेश, अस्, m.,
N. of the tenth chapter of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the
Śiva-Purāṇa.

दाक्षायणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having gold, wearing
golden ornaments; (ई), m. a Brāhman student wear-
ing golden ear-rings.

दाक्षायण्य, अस्, m. the son of the Dākṣā
yaṇī Aditi, the sun.
दाक्षायिणी, f. wrong form for दाक्षायणी above.

दाक्षेय, अस्, m. ‘the son of Dākṣī,’ a metro-
nymic of Pāṇini; (ई), f. ‘the daughter of Dākṣī (?).’

दाक्ष्य, अम्, n. cleverness, dexterity, skill, abi-
lity, capability, fitness; probity, integrity.

दाक्षिणात्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दक्षिणा, ind.),
southerly, southern, belonging to or produced in
the south; belonging to or living in the Dekhan,
situated in the Dekhan; दाक्षिणात्या भाषा, the
language spoken in the south; (अस्), m., N. of a
preceptor mentioned in the Ānanda-laharī; the cocoa-
nut; (अस्, अम्), m. or n. (?), the south; (आस्), m. pl.
the inhabitants of the Dekhan; N. of several precep-
tors mentioned in the Kāma-sūtra by Vātsyāyana.

दाक्षिणिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दक्षिणा), connected
with a sacrificial gift.
